title: The Orbital Frontier: Managing Space Debris
subtitle: An examination of the growing crisis in Earth's orbit and the global efforts to secure a sustainable future in space.
description: As humanity relies increasingly on satellite technology for communication and navigation, the accumulation of space debris threatens the future of space exploration. This series explores the history, stakeholders, and emerging policies shaping the management of our orbital environment.

articles.label: Part 1
articles.note: Explain the historical accumulation of debris and the theoretical 'Kessler Syndrome' tipping point.

articles.label: Part 2
articles.note: Identify the key players: national space agencies, private satellite constellations (like Starlink), and the emerging 'space cleanup' industry.

articles.label: Part 3
articles.note: Discuss the impact of Anti-Satellite (ASAT) tests and the recent shift toward international guidelines for 'responsible space behavior'.

articles.label: Part 4
articles.note: Analyze the economic and societal impacts, including increased insurance premiums and risks to essential services like GPS.

articles.label: Part 5
articles.note: Explore emerging technologies for 'Active Debris Removal' (ADR) and the unresolved legal questions of ownership.
